transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-29 14:00 UTC / Duration: 37m / Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Leah (Redwood SE), Ivy (Redwood CSM); Marcus (OpalShift CTO), Ana (Lead ML Eng), Devon (Infra), Priya (Security)

Summary: Quick discovery for a small pilot - OpalShift wants to try Redwood self-serve API with trial credits, evaluate hosted vs dedicated vs VPC/p private pilot. Key concerns: data residency, KMS integration, latency p99, cost per 1k tokens. Agreed next: credits and docs, technical demo, pilot scope.

00:00 Samir (Redwood): Hey everybody thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. Quick roll call, and then I want to understand your immediate goal for a two week pilot.
00:15 Marcus (OpalShift): Hey Samir, yep Marcus here. We're trying to get from prototype to production-ish, specifically a question answering service over customer docs. We want to prove latency and cost at scale and also validate security.
00:30 Leah (Redwood SE): Great, Marcus. A couple quick questions up front — what stack are you planning to run from? Is this going to be client-side? server-side? cloud provider?
00:45 Ana (OpalShift): Server-side. Most of our infra is AWS us-east-1. We have a microservice that will call the API. Primary models will be open models similar to Llama-family but we can be flexible.
01:00 Devon (OpalShift): We also have an existing in-house GPU infra but it's more for training; we don't have a production inference stack.
01:12 Samir (Redwood): Cool — so there are two routes: self-serve hosted API for fastest time-to-first-call and reserved/dedicated or private VPC if you need isolation. For a two week pilot we usually recommend starting with hosted and our free credits so you get to first-token quickly.
01:30 Priya (OpalShift, Security): Quick interruption — we need to vet SOC2, encryption at rest with customer KMS, and audit logs. Can hosted satisfy that for a pilot?
01:45 Leah (Redwood): Yes, hosted covers a lot. We have SOC2 Type II and support customer-managed keys via KMS for Private deployments; for hosted we offer encryption at rest and in-transit, and we can provide detailed audit logs. For pilots that require KMS we usually do a VPC/private pilot, but we can also provide more narrow data controls for hosted as an interim step.
02:10 Marcus: When you say "detailed audit logs" is that per-request with tokens or just aggregate?
02:20 Ivy (Redwood CSM): We can surface request-level metadata and token-level billing, but not raw prompt text in standard retention — we can provide session IDs and traces. We'll share the security spreadsheet link after the call.
02:35 Devon: Would you be able to route calls out of us-east-1? We want to reduce latency to our users in NA East.
02:45 Leah: Yes, our hosted endpoints have region routing; we can spin up near your VPC. If you want dedicated reserved capacity, that's pinned and gives you steady p99s. For hosted we see typical p50/p95/p99 numbers in our perf deck — I'll link that.
03:05 Samir: For time-to-first-token (TTFT), we see customers go from signup to first request in under an hour if they use our quickstart SDK and example prompts. The free credits cover basic usage for the two-week pilot.
03:20 Ana: About credits, do you limit model choice? We're hoping to experiment with a couple of different open weights and maybe run 8-bit quantized variants.
03:35 Samir: No hard model lock. The hosted catalog includes a set of curated models and quantized variants. For experiments we can enable model variants in your trial account. We'll note that for the proposal.
03:50 Marcus: Cost — we need rough per-1k-token numbers to budget. Ballpark?
04:00 Leah: Ballpark depends heavily on model and sequence length. For a small dense open model family you might see $0.15-$1.00 per 1k tokens; for larger variants more. We'll include examples in the pricing sheet. Also batching and KV caching reduce per-token cost.
04:25 Ana: KV caching — do you do automatic prefix caching? We have a lot of repeated context in queries.
04:33 Leah: Yes, we have prefix/KV cache support in the runtime and the platform can handle transparent cache reuse which cuts both latency and cost for repetitive prompts. We'll propose caching settings for your workload.
04:50 Priya: On the private side, what is the difference between Dedicated and Private? The terms are confusing in our procurement doc.
05:00 Samir: Good question. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in our managed infra that are tenant-isolated but still in Redwood's control plane. Private is a VPC or on-prem deployment where the control plane can be customer-managed and KMS/HSM integrations are available for stronger compliance. Dedicated has faster onboarding than Private but both give better isolation than hosted.
05:20 Devon: For the pilot, what's the typical lead time for dedicated or private?
05:28 Samir: Dedicated — if capacity is available — can be 2-4 weeks. Private (VPC) typically 4-8 weeks depending on network and KMS integrations. Hosted trial is immediate.
05:40 Marcus: Ok hosted for now then. We'll be conservative on data — PII redaction will be done client side.
05:48 Ivy: That works, and we'll keep logs scoped as you require. We'll add a step with Priya to align on data retention.
06:00 Ana: A technical question — what about latency SLOs and throttling? If we have spikes can you auto-fallback to cheaper model variants?
06:10 Leah: Yes, we have smart routing and fallback policies. You can define per-route policies that prefer lower-latency variants or cheaper ones. During spikes you can also enable our burst capacity to absorb short spikes.
06:25 Marcus: Wonderful. Can we run a small benchmark — say 1000 requests with 1k tokens each — to measure cost and p99?
06:35 Leah: Absolutely. For the pilot we'd recommend a representative prompt set of 100-200 prompts and run them across three model variants. We'll measure throughput, latency, and cost. We can run this from your infra or from Redwood to get a direct comparison.
06:55 Devon: If Redwood runs it, will it see our prompts? Is that a problem for security?
07:05 Leah: We can run the benchmark against synthetic prompts or sanitized samples you provide, and we'll sign the NDA-protected data usage for pilot purposes.
07:18 Priya: On SSO and provisioning — does Redwood support SAML/SCIM for user provisioning into the console?
07:26 Samir: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning and RBAC. For pilot you'll be Admin invited or we can set up SSO.
07:36 Marcus: Good. Operationally, what's the observability like? Tracing? per-request token breakdown?
07:45 Ivy: Console shows token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, traces for errors, and you can export logs to your SIEM. We'll share a screenshot in the follow up.
07:58 Ana: How often do people run into quality regressions when switching to quantized models? We're worried about hallucinations increasing with 4-bit quantized variants.
08:10 Leah: It depends on model and task. We run eval suites tied to prompt sets and can recommend quantization profiles based on your LLM workload. For QA tasks, we often keep a larger float model behind a canary. The Optimize toolkit suggests safe quant profiles.
08:30 Marcus: That sounds reasonable. For the trial scope — we want: 1) set up hosted trial with credits, 2) run the benchmark (100-200 prompts across 3 variants), 3) have a short SE demo of routing/caching and console. Timeline: two weeks. Ok?
08:50 Samir: Sounds good. We'll aim to provision credits today/tomorrow and schedule the SE demo for early next week.
09:00 Priya: Please include the security docs link in the follow up. Also we may want to invite procurement later if we go dedicated.
09:10 Samir: Will do. I'll put the links and pricing in email and cc Ivy.

(brief cross-talk, logistics)

24:25 Leah: Quick note on integration — SDKs are in Python, Node, and a generic HTTP client. Our quickstart repo has a one-file example that hits the generation endpoint and streams tokens. That usually gets teams to first-token in ~15 minutes if they follow the guide.
24:45 Ana: Perfect, that'll help. We prefer Python for the microservice.
25:00 Samir: Ok next steps recap: Samir sends trial credits + pricing sheet + security doc links; Leah schedules a technical demo and prepares benchmark plan; Ivy shares quickstart repo. OpalShift to share sanitized prompt set and compliance checklist.
25:28 Marcus: We'll try to have that prompt set by Thursday — two day turnaround.
25:35 Priya: One more question — does Redwood support customer-side token masking or redaction at the edge?
25:42 Leah: We recommend redaction client-side; we also provide enterprise hooks for request transformation in private deployments. We'll include patterns in the security doc.
25:55 Samir: Great — I think that's a wrap. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the links and proposed dates.
26:05 Devon: Thanks all.
26:08 Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions: "KV cache" written as "K V cash" in some ASR lines, "SOC2" shows as "sock two" several times. Speaker attributions may be approximate early in the call.

End of meeting.
